From: Rob Castellano
To: All Employees
Date: Fri, 2 Feb 2024 07:45
Subject: ApexHip market withdrawal announcement

Team,

This morning we announced a voluntary market withdrawal of ApexHip, effective immediately. This decision was reviewed and approved by the Board.

Over the past several years we have continued to monitor registry data, including the NJR and AJRR reporting on ApexHip's revision rates. That data has continued to evolve, and after further review with our clinical and regulatory leadership, we've concluded that withdrawing the product now is the right thing to do out of an abundance of caution for patient safety. This is not a step we take lightly, given how many patients and surgeons have relied on ApexHip.

Sales and Regulatory Affairs will be receiving detailed guidance today on next steps, including customer communications, inventory handling, and case-by-case surgeon support. Please hold off on any independent outreach to customers or press until you've received that guidance.

If you have questions, please route them to Dana Okonkwo's team in Regulatory Affairs. Please do not speak to media or plaintiffs' counsel directly — refer any such inquiries to Legal.

I know this is a significant change. Thank you for your professionalism as we work through it together.

Rob

Northgate Health System
Attn: Risk Management / Materials Management
Re: URGENT — Voluntary Recall Notification
ApexHip Acetabular Cup, Lots V-2200 through V-2299
FDA Recall Number: Z-1418-2022

Dear Risk Management Colleague:

This letter serves as formal notification that Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. is voluntarily recalling ApexHip acetabular cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured at our Cork, Ireland facility between November 2021 and February 2022. This action has been classified by FDA as a Class II recall under recall number Z-1418-2022.

This recall was initiated after incoming inspection at two hospital sites identified flaking of the KinetiCoat porous titanium coating upon unwrapping of the sterile package, prior to implantation. Our investigation determined that a plasma-spray process parameter drift, following a chamber maintenance event, resulted in inconsistent coating adhesion in the affected lots. To date, 1,140 units from these lots have been distributed, with approximately 412 implanted.

We are asking that Northgate Health System take the following actions immediately:

1. Identify and quarantine all remaining unimplanted units from lots V-2200 through V-2299 in your inventory.
2. Do not use quarantined units for surgical procedures.
3. Complete the enclosed Effectiveness Check Response Form, documenting your inventory review, and return it to our Regulatory Affairs department within 10 business days of the date of this letter.
4. Contact your Veridian sales representative or Customer Quality at 1-800-555-0142 to arrange return and replacement of quarantined stock at no cost.

If any implanted patients have experienced adverse events potentially related to coating integrity, please report these through your standard adverse event process and notify our Complaint Handling department as well.

We regret any disruption this may cause and appreciate your prompt cooperation. Please contact me directly with any questions.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
VP, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.
dokonkwo@veridianortho.com

From: Dana Okonkwo
To: Priya Raman; Devon Mitchell
Date: Fri, 7 Sep 2018 09:47
Subject: RE: Atlanta cluster - MDR reportability question

Priya,

Agree this warrants a documented look rather than an informal call and close. My preliminary view, subject to Devon's analysis below:

Under 21 CFR 803.50(a), a report is required if we become aware of information reasonably suggesting the device (1) may have caused or contributed to a death or serious injury, or (2) has malfunctioned and would be likely to cause or contribute to a death or serious injury if the malfunction recurred. Elevated serum cobalt alone, without a confirmed malfunction (e.g., coating failure, wear debris finding) or a confirmed serious injury (e.g., biopsy-confirmed ARMD, revision), does not on its face meet either prong. Lab values trending high can reflect normal wear within expected ranges.

That said, three complaints from one practice in a short window is the kind of pattern that deserves a written analysis, not just a verbal judgment call.

Next steps:

1. Devon - please run the formal 803.50(a) reportability analysis on all three TrackWise records (get me the TW IDs), including whether any imaging or biopsy findings exist.
2. Priya - confirm current cobalt/chromium values and reference ranges used by Dr. Feld's office; note any prior revision history for these three patients.
3. Devon - prepare draft MDR filings in parallel, to be held pending the analysis, in case the conclusion shifts.
4. Both - document the rationale in the file regardless of outcome, including the "not reportable at this time" determination if that's where we land.

Let's reconvene once Devon has a first pass. Thanks both.

Dana

MEMORANDUM

TO: Confidential Personnel File / Operations Leadership
FROM: Lisa Tran, HR Business Partner, R&D and Quality / Manufacturing Operations
DATE: June 20, 2022
SUBJECT: Performance Evaluation Supplement — Bill Kowalski (Plant Manager, Cork) — Q2 2022

Purpose
This memorandum serves as an off-cycle performance addendum to Bill Kowalski’s annual review cycle in Workday, documenting extraordinary operational leadership and crisis management at the Cork manufacturing facility during the first half of June 2022.

Context & Incident Response
Following reports from Northgate Health System and an account in Denver regarding packaging-level KinetiCoat adhesion issues on ApexHip acetabular cups, Veridian initiated a voluntary Class II recall on June 14, 2022 (FDA Recall No. Z-1418-2022), covering lot series V-2200 through V-2299.

Upon notification, Bill immediately halted line 3 operations in Cork and mobilized his manufacturing engineering team to conduct an exhaustive trace across chamber batch records dating from November 2021 through February 2022. Within 72 hours, Bill successfully isolated the root cause: plasma-spray parameter drift linked directly to a recalibration discrepancy following scheduled vacuum chamber maintenance in early November. His direct technical oversight enabled the containment of unaffected lots and prevented broader inventory quarantines across the EU and US supply pipelines.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
Throughout the escalation, Bill demonstrated exemplary cross-functional coordination. He worked closely with Priya Raman (Director, Quality & Complaint Handling) to validate TrackWise containment protocols and reconcile batch traveler discrepancies against physical scrap counts. Furthermore, he partnered directly with Dana Okonkwo (VP Regulatory Affairs) to ensure that the production data, machine maintenance logs, and distribution reconciliations provided to FDA CDRH were fully substantiated and auditable on tight statutory turnaround times.

Bill’s transparent communication and calm demeanor under severe operational pressure minimized plant downtime and maintained morale across the Cork machining and coating shifts.

Recommendation
In recognition of Bill’s rapid root-cause identification, meticulous line containment, and collaborative support during the voluntary recall execution, I strongly recommend a discretionary spot bonus of $10,000, along with a formal commendation entered into his permanent Workday profile.

Submitted by:
*Lisa Tran*
HR Business Partner, R&D, Quality & Global Operations

MEMORANDUM

TO: Dana Okonkwo (VP, Regulatory Affairs), Rachel Steinberg (General Counsel), Dr. Leon Adeyemi (Chief Medical Officer), Marcus Lee (VP, Sales)
FROM: Carlos Mendes (Product Manager, ApexHip)
DATE: September 28, 2021
SUBJECT: Draft "Dear Doctor" Letter – ApexHip Acetabular System Labeling Update

Following the decisions reached during our September 14 Registry Signal Review meeting, I have prepared the initial draft text for the upcoming customer notification ("Dear Doctor" letter) regarding the ApexHip Total Hip System.

As agreed by the review team and executive leadership, Veridian will maintain active commercial distribution of ApexHip while implementing an immediate Instructions for Use (IFU) labeling update to address emerging registry trends.

Background & Signal Summary
The primary driver for this communication is data presented from the March 2021 National Joint Registry (NJR) 17th Annual Report, which identified a cumulative 5-year revision rate of 7.1% for the ApexHip construct, compared to an average class benchmark of approximately 3.2% across contemporary metal-on-metal (MoM) hip resurfacing and total replacement systems. While internal clinical evaluations indicate that well-positioned constructs continue to demonstrate strong clinical survivorship, registry data and internal engineering assessments correlate early revisions predominantly with adverse local tissue reactions (ALTR/ARMD) linked to elevated cobalt and chromium ion levels.

Proposed Letter Content & Labeling Guidance
The draft notification emphasizes patient safety, precise surgical technique, and targeted post-operative vigilance:

1. Patient Monitoring Recommendations: We advise clinicians to establish heightened routine clinical and radiographic follow-up protocols for all implanted ApexHip patients, with particular attention to individuals receiving larger femoral head diameters (≥44 mm). Routine cross-sectional imaging (MARS-MRI or ultrasound) and periodic blood metal-ion quantification (whole blood cobalt and chromium) should be considered annually or upon any presentation of unexplained pain, clicking, or swelling.
2. Surgical Positioning & Angle Inclination: Revisions strongly correlate with edge-loading phenomena. The revised labeling explicitly instructs surgeons to target an acetabular cup inclination angle within 40° to 45° and anteversion between 15° and 20°. Operating outside these ranges—specifically exceeding 50° of operative abduction—markedly increases the risk of accelerated fluid-film wear and premature component loosening.

Next Steps & Timeline
Our target mail date to all US and EU implanting orthopedic surgeons, chief medical officers, and relevant risk management personnel is mid-October 2021. Reps will receive accompanying talking points once this text is locked.

Please review the attached formal notification layout (`Apex_Dear_Doctor_Draft_v1.docx`) and provide your redlines. We require formal sign-off from Regulatory Affairs, Legal, and Clinical before Dana submits the final package to the agency and we proceed with mass distribution.

MEMORANDUM

FROM: Greg Novak (Director, Post-Market Surveillance)

SUBJECT: NJR 2021 Annual Report – ApexHip 5-Year Revision Rate Analysis

Executive Summary

The UK National Joint Registry (NJR) has released its 2021 Annual Report data tables, incorporating cumulative implant survival figures through December 31, 2020.

Our initial data extraction for the ApexHip Total Hip System reveals a statistically significant adverse survival divergence. The cumulative 5-year revision rate for ApexHip is reported at 7.1% (95% CI: 6.2%–8.1%), compared to a class benchmark of 3.2% (95% CI: 3.0%–3.4%) across contemporaneous metal-on-metal (MoM) and hybrid construct cohorts in the registry.

Cohort Breakdown and Timing of Divergence

The NJR dataset captures 4,128 primary ApexHip procedures performed across UK centers since CE mark entry in September 2017:

*   Total Implants Tracked: 4,128 units (primarily 48mm–54mm acetabular cup sizes paired with matching Co/Cr femoral heads).
*   Total Revisions Recorded: 184 cases.
*   Revision Rate Trajectory:
    *   *Year 1:* 1.2% (ApexHip) vs. 0.9% (Class average)
    *   *Year 2:* 2.4% (ApexHip) vs. 1.7% (Class average)
    *   *Year 3:* 4.6% (ApexHip) vs. 2.3% (Class average)
    *   *Year 5:* 7.1% (ApexHip) vs. 3.2% (Class average)

The performance curve begins to diverge distinctly between months 24 and 36. Primary indications cited for revision within the NJR return entries include "pain of unknown origin," "aseptic loosening/cup migration," and "adverse soft tissue reaction" (accounting for roughly 48% of coded revision rationales past the 36-month mark).

Next Steps & Recommendations

1.  AJRR Cross-Validation: We must correlate these findings against domestic performance immediately. American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) annual procedural datasets are slated for release later in 2021. I strongly recommend we prepare an identical query syntax to interrogate US revision trajectories as soon as that raw data cuts become available.
2.  Clinical Assessment: I request Dr. Adeyemi’s formal clinical read regarding whether a 7.1% 5-year cumulative revision rate crosses our established Post-Market Clinical Follow-up (PMCF) internal action thresholds, particularly given the elevated proportion of soft-tissue and aseptic indications.
3.  Formal Signal Review: Under our post-market surveillance SOPs, this variance warrants convening an interdepartmental Registry Signal Review meeting among Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Clinical, and Product Engineering to determine if labeling amendments, field communications, or formal CAPA escalation are required.

Please let me know your availability later this week to discuss these initial figures.

Re: Voluntary Recall Notification - ApexHip Acetabular Cup Lots V-2200 to V-2299
FDA Recall No. Z-1418-2022

To Whom It May Concern:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. hereby notifies the Food and Drug Administration of a voluntary Class II recall of specified ApexHip acetabular cup lots. The affected devices are ApexHip cobalt/chromium acetabular cups with KinetiCoat porous titanium coating, manufactured at Veridian’s Cork, Ireland facility.

The recall applies to cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured from November 2021 through February 2022. A total of 1,140 units were distributed in the United States. Based on the current lot-trace reconciliation, 412 units have been implanted. The balance is located in customer or distributor inventory, has been returned, or remains in Veridian-controlled inventory pending final reconciliation.

The recall was initiated following incoming-inspection reports from two hospital customers, including Northgate Health System and a Denver-area hospital. In each report, flaking of the KinetiCoat coating was observed upon removal of the device from its packaging. No other ApexHip lots are included in this action.

Veridian’s investigation has identified plasma-spray parameter drift following a chamber maintenance event at the Cork facility as the probable root cause of the coating adhesion failures. Review of applicable batch records, chamber data, and maintenance documentation supports this conclusion. The investigation remains open, and Veridian will provide supplemental information should additional findings affect the scope or assessment of this action.

Immediate corrective actions include: (1) cessation of distribution for the affected lots; (2) segregation and inventory reconciliation of affected product; (3) inspection and requalification of the plasma-spray chamber; (4) verification of plasma-spray operating parameters and associated monitoring controls; and (5) review and revision, as appropriate, of maintenance and post-maintenance release procedures. The chamber will not be returned to routine production until requalification requirements have been completed and approved by Quality.

Customer notification letters are being sent concurrently to all known consignees, with instructions to identify, cease use of, and return affected product. Veridian will conduct effectiveness checks and provide periodic status reports in accordance with FDA requirements.

This action concerns a coating adhesion issue and is not related to metal-ion wear or other field performance concerns associated with ApexHip.

Please contact me at (574) 555-0142 or dokonkwo@veridianortho.com with any questions.

Sincerely,

Dana Okonkwo
Vice President, Regulatory Affairs
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

3. EVENT NARRATIVE

Dr. Whitaker reported that patient JW-1102 presented with progressive groin pain, swelling, and reduced range of motion approximately three years after primary implantation. Pre-revision laboratory testing reportedly showed elevated cobalt levels; the surgeon reported serum cobalt of 12.4 µg/L. Based on information presently available, metal-on-metal bearing wear and associated metal debris are suspected contributors to the elevated metal-ion findings and local tissue reaction. MEMORANDUM

To: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Date: June 30, 2020
Subject: ApexHip Complaint Trending Report - H1 2020

This memorandum summarizes ApexHip complaint activity entered in TrackWise from January 1 through June 30, 2020. The review was conducted per the approved complaint trending procedure and includes complaints received from direct customer contacts, sales representatives, distributors, and surgeon offices. Duplicate reports concerning the same patient event were consolidated where identified.

A total of 68 ApexHip complaints were logged during H1 2020. Of these, 31 complaints relate to elevated cobalt and/or chromium ion values, suspected adverse reaction to metal debris (ARMD), unexplained pain with metal-on-metal bearing concerns, or imaging findings that may be consistent with local tissue reaction. This compares with 19 complaints in the corresponding H1 2019 period.

The increase is notable, although several of the 2020 reports concern implants placed in 2017 and 2018 and therefore reflect a growing population of implants with longer follow-up. The reports are geographically dispersed, with no single account or surgeon responsible for a majority of the entries. Atlanta remains a higher-volume source of reports, but this is not materially different from its overall Apex utilization.

Lot review was completed for complaints where component lot information was available. The implicated cups, stems, and heads span multiple manufacturing periods and component lots. No individual cup lot, stem lot, or head lot represents a meaningful concentration of the metal-ion/ARMD-related complaints. In particular, there is no repeated lot pattern that would support a discrete manufacturing containment action at this time. The current distribution is more consistent with a wear-related or use-condition-related pattern than with a single manufacturing-related event. This conclusion should remain provisional pending receipt of additional implant and surgical-positioning information.

Nine events in the H1 population involve confirmed revision surgery. Explant analysis has been completed or preliminarily reviewed for seven of those cases; the remaining two explants are either with the hospital pathology department or pending return to Veridian. The available analyses describe polished wear areas, linear or arcuate surface scars, and in several cases damage patterns at the cup rim/head interface. Where operative records and radiographs were provided, the cases generally involved higher reported cup inclination angles.

These observations are consistent with the elevated-angle wear concern previously identified in the 2019 engineering re-analysis. As discussed at the time, the standard test configuration did not evaluate all surgical orientations observed in clinical practice. Quality is not making a causal determination based on complaint data alone; however, the alignment between the explant observations and the prior wear-test findings warrants continued close monitoring.

MDR assessments have been completed for all reportable events received through the reporting cutoff. Required submissions have been made within the applicable timelines, and the MDR log is current as of June 30. A small number of files remain open for follow-up medical records and device-return information, but no reportable event is presently overdue for evaluation or filing.

Recommended actions are as follows:

1. Continue monthly ApexHip complaint trending, with a separate review of metal-ion, ARMD, and revision events.
2. Maintain enhanced follow-up requests for radiographs, cup inclination information, metal-ion laboratory values, and explant returns.
3. Provide the updated trend data to Post-Market Surveillance for comparison against available registry data.
4. Reassess whether escalation to a formal cross-functional signal review is appropriate if the current reporting rate continues through Q3.

Legal has been informally briefed regarding the volume increase and the nature of the allegations. No change to the current complaint-handling procedure is proposed at this time.

Priya

ENGINEERING MEMORANDUM

Date: March 10, 2022
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Subject: Explant analysis summary - Whitaker case, lot V-2114

This memo summarizes Engineering’s visual and materials review of the retrieved ApexHip femoral head and acetabular cup from the revision performed by Dr. James Whitaker in Denver. The components were received at Warsaw on February 28, 2022, under return authorization RA-22-0317. The cup is identified as lot V-2114. Component identifiers on the returned head are consistent with the operative record supplied by Dr. Whitaker’s office.

The case materials indicate revision after persistent pain, elevated serum cobalt and chromium values, and imaging findings described by the treating team as concerning for an adverse local tissue reaction. I am not making a clinical determination from the device examination; that remains for the treating physician and Clinical/Quality. The observations below are limited to the returned components and associated debris sample.

Visual examination of the bearing surfaces found circumferential polishing on the femoral head, with the more pronounced damage localized to a band corresponding to the superior-lateral cup rim. The cup bearing surface has directional wear striations extending inward from the rim at approximately the 11 to 2 o’clock positions when oriented to the surgeon’s orientation marks. There is also a narrow area of matte discoloration and scratching at the rim transition. The pattern is not consistent with uniform, concentric articulation under nominal orientation.

The available postoperative radiograph supplied with the case file appears to place the cup at a relatively high inclination angle. Exact measurement should be confirmed by Clinical or the treating site, but the apparent orientation is in the range where edge contact becomes more likely.

This is materially similar to the pattern we saw in the 2019 55-degree inclination reruns. In that work, once the contact patch migrated toward the cup rim, wear increased substantially and the resulting head/cup surface damage was directional rather than evenly distributed. The retrieved surfaces here show the same basic mechanism: rim contact/edge loading followed by localized abrasive wear.

Materials analysis of the collected particulate residue identified cobalt/chromium-containing debris. Quantitation from the digestion sample was 18.6 µg cobalt and 7.9 µg chromium per gram of recovered residue. Those values should not be read as a direct measure of total in vivo burden, given recovery limitations and handling at revision, but the composition and relative concentration are consistent with the elevated serum ion readings reported in the case materials.

No coating delamination was observed on the accessible KinetiCoat exterior surface, and this does not appear related to the Cork coating issue associated with the V-2200 series lots. V-2114 is outside that population.

My conclusion is that the retrieval findings are consistent with the known edge-loading wear mechanism at high cup inclination, with associated Co/Cr debris generation. Quality should add this case to the cumulative metal-ion complaint dataset and include it in the next MDR trending review. I recommend retaining the components and microscopy images with the complaint file; Engineering has retained the raw photos and measurement worksheet in the Apex retrieval folder.

Tom Halvorsen
Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip

Subject: Retrospective audit results - ApexHip complaint files 2018-2020

Priya,

Per our commitment in the July 483 response regarding Observation 2 (complaint trending and reporting timeliness), I completed the retrospective review of closed ApexHip files from the 2018–2020 period.

In total, I sampled 84 files tagged with metal-ion elevation, pain, or early loosening. The vast majority adhered strictly to SOP-QA-402 and the MDR decision tree. However, I flagged two specific files from the initial August 2018 Atlanta cluster out of Dr. Marcus Feld’s practice that warrant additional documentation:

- TW-2018-0842 (bilateral patient, elevated cobalt/chromium, mild swelling)
- TW-2018-0855 (pain, elevated ions, revision discussed but postponed pending imaging)

There is a defensible argument that based on initial correspondence with Feld’s clinical coordinator, these should have been escalated for formal 30-day MDR determination sooner than the 60-day mark when the revision surgeries were formally scheduled. Ultimately, under our existing decision tree criteria (Form RA-104), neither case met the threshold for reportable serious injury at initial intake because no medical intervention was immediately required beyond routine surveillance and blood work.

While the ultimate decision not to file MDRs at that initial contact stage was technically defensible under 21 CFR 803.3, the file notes are thin on why the 30-day clock wasn’t triggered upon the receipt of the lab results.

My recommendation is that we add an addendum memo to both TrackWise records clearly articulating the retrospective rationale and alignment with the decision tree. Having that explicit documentation in place will ensure we are completely solid if Delgado or another investigator asks to see the remediated audit samples during the follow-up inspection.

Let me know if you want me to route the draft notes for your sign-off.

Best,

Devon Mitchell
Sr. Regulatory Specialist

SUBJECT: Response to Additional Information Request – ApexHip™ Total Hip System (510(k) K162447) Medical Device Reporting (MDR) Trending Inquiry

Dear Dr. Anand:

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. ("Veridian") submits this response to the Additional Information (AI) request issued by the Office of Compliance on May 8, 2019, regarding MDR reporting trends and post-market complaint volume associated with the ApexHip Total Hip System (K162447).

We have conducted a thorough review of our post-market surveillance data, internal complaint files in TrackWise, and corresponding MDR filings submitted pursuant to 21 CFR Part 803 for the period covering January 1, 2018 through April 30, 2019.

Based on our analysis, Veridian provides the following clarifications and commitments:

1. Complaint Rate vs. Sales Volume: The absolute increase in complaint and MDR submissions noted in your correspondence correlates directly with rapid post-market commercial adoption rather than an underlying product defect. Specifically, our cumulative complaint rate across all distributed lots for the trailing twelve months stands at 0.29% of implanted units, compared to 0.24% observed during the prior twelve-month period. When normalized against our commercial implant volume—which grew substantially throughout 2018—the overall complaint rate remains consistent with industry benchmarks for large-diameter metal-on-metal systems.

2. Engineering Evaluation: In response to specific clinical feedback alleging localized tissue responses and revision procedures, Veridian initiated an internal engineering evaluation to further examine tribological wear characteristics and implant orientation dynamics. This engineering review remains ongoing under our Quality System procedures (21 CFR Part 820).

3. Follow-Up Reporting: Veridian will continue rigorous monitoring of post-market clinical performance. Should adverse trend signals persist or exceed established internal control limits, Veridian commits to providing CDRH with a comprehensive follow-up summary report in Q4 2019 detailing the findings of our ongoing wear evaluation and complaint investigations.

Please contact the undersigned at (574) 555-0140 or via email at dokonkwo@veridianortho.com should you require additional documentation or have further questions.

Subject: Claim substantiation review - Q2 sales deck slide 14

Anika, Carlos,

I completed my clinical review of the updated Q2 ApexHip sales collateral deck from Kessler Reid. Most of the revisions to the "Active Life" positioning look reasonable, but I cannot sign off on slide 14 in its current form.

The graphic compares ApexHip’s revision rate favorably against Stryker’s Trident/Accolade construct, asserting superior mid-term survivorship. However, looking closely at the footnotes, our bar is pulled from our internal 2-year post-market surveillance cohort (n=412), whereas the comparator bar cites published registry data tracking patients out to 5 years.

Juxtaposing a 2-year cumulative revision curve against a 5-year benchmark is clinically invalid and frankly misleading. As implant survivorship curves inevitably decline over time, this is not an apples-to-apples comparison and will not withstand regulatory or clinical scrutiny from hospital VAC committees.

Please either pull slide 14 entirely from the distribution deck or adjust the graphic so that both cohorts reflect matched follow-up durations (ideally citing standardized 2-year registry intervals) with the respective timeframes prominently labeled.

Best regards,

Leon

MEMORANDUM

Veridian Orthopedics, Inc. — Quality Assurance

Date: August 15, 2019
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
To: File / Distribution per QA-SOP-014
Re: Quarterly Complaint Trending Summary — ApexHip, Q2 2019

Purpose

This memo summarizes complaint trending for the ApexHip system for Q2 2019 (April–June), per procedure QA-SOP-014 (Complaint Trending and Analysis).

Summary of Complaint Volume

A total of 11 complaints were logged in TrackWise for ApexHip during Q2 2019, up from 8 in Q1 2019. Of these, 7 complaints involved reports of elevated metal ion (Co/Cr) levels and/or early revision surgery, compared to 5 such complaints in Q1 2019. This represents a continued upward trend in metal-ion-related complaints over the last two quarters.

Complaints by region (metal-ion/revision subset, n=7):

| Region | Count |
|---|---|
| Southeast | 6 |
| Northeast | 2 |
| Midwest | 3 |

(Note: table totals to 11 as it reflects overall regional distribution for all Q2 complaints, not only the metal-ion subset; Southeast figure includes 4 metal-ion-related cases.)

Per record review, the majority of the affected implants trace to index surgeries performed in 2017–2018, consistent with prior quarters' pattern. Surgeon of record was identified in all cases; no single implanting surgeon accounts for a disproportionate share this quarter, though the Southeast region continues to represent the largest single source, consistent with Dr. Feld's practice volume in that territory.

MDR Assessment

Each complaint was individually evaluated per 21 CFR 803.50 reportability criteria. Per procedure, none of the seven metal-ion/revision complaints, taken individually, meets the threshold for mandatory reporting — none reflects a malfunction that would be likely to cause or contribute to death or serious injury if it were to recur, based on available clinical documentation at this time. Individual determinations are documented in the respective TrackWise records (TW-2019-0398 through TW-2019-0441, non-consecutive).

Trend Assessment and Recommendation

While individual complaints do not independently trigger MDR obligations, the quarter-over-quarter increase (5 to 7 in the metal-ion/revision category) is notable and, per QA-SOP-014 Section 6.2, warrants continued close monitoring going into Q3. I am recommending that this trend be flagged for consideration of a formal CAPA, given the consistency of the pattern across regions and the concentration of affected units in the 2017–2018 surgical cohort.

I also recommend coordination with Design Engineering (Tom Halvorsen) regarding the wear-testing findings at 55-degree cup inclination completed earlier this year, as several of the revision cases reference elevated inclination angles noted intraoperatively. A joint review may help clarify whether device-related factors are contributing to the observed trend, or whether this remains within expected variation for the surgical population.

This summary will be provided to Regulatory Affairs (D. Okonkwo) for awareness and to Post-Market Surveillance (G. Novak) for inclusion in the next registry data comparison.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

Priya, Carlos,

Finished the re-run I mentioned a few weeks back. Wanted to test the cup at 55 degrees inclination instead of the standard 45 we used for the original 14242 protocol, just to see what happens outside the "ideal" implant orientation, since we know a chunk of surgeons run steeper than textbook.

Results aren't good. Wear rates at 55 deg are running 4-6x what we see at 45 deg, consistently across the three cup sizes I tested. Attached is the raw data and summary charts - Apex_wear_55deg_rev2.xlsx. Take a look at the tab labeled "edge loading summary," that's where it's most obvious.

This is bugging me because if surgeons are landing cups anywhere near 55 deg in practice, we'd expect elevated metal release from edge loading, and that lines up uncomfortably well with the complaint clusters we've seen out of Atlanta and Nashville - the cobalt/chromium numbers on a few of those patients were high enough that people noticed. I'm not saying that's definitely what's happening, but it's not nothing either.

Priya - given FDA is already asking us about MDR trending, does this need to go up to regulatory? Feels like something Dana should at least know about before it comes up on its own. Tom

Rachel, Hannah—

A brief recap from today’s call with Aegis Specialty, including their coverage team and our broker.

Aegis did not provide a formal written coverage determination, but their stated position was that the current ApexHip ARMD claims would fall under one products-hazard aggregate limit of $50M. Their view appears to be that the alleged injuries arise from a common product issue and therefore aggregate notwithstanding different implant dates, surgeons, or jurisdictions.

That is materially less favorable than the approach we discussed internally. They also made clear that the February market withdrawal does not change their aggregation analysis.

For planning purposes, we are carrying a $45M Apex-related claims reserve at present. With filed and threatened claim volume continuing to rise, the practical concern is that we could be approaching the stated aggregate limit within the year. That assumes, of course, Aegis maintains this position and the claims develop at anything close to current rates.

Rachel: please assess whether we should retain coverage counsel to challenge the aggregation position now, rather than wait for a denial or exhaustion notice. I would appreciate your recommendation on timing, likely cost, and whether there is a meaningful argument under the policy language.

Hannah: please run a downside scenario in which self-funded exposure rises above $30M, with sensitivity at $35M and $50M. Include expected timing by quarter, cash impact, and any implications for the 2024 forecast and disclosures. Please separate defense costs if the available data permits; Aegis was not clear today whether it considers those inside or outside the limit.

Let’s take this offline after Rachel has reviewed the policy and Hannah has a first pass.

Owen

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
QUALITY & COMPLAINT HANDLING MEMORANDUM

Date: June 22, 2020
From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Subject: KneeFlex Complaint Trend Summary Q2 2020

This memorandum summarizes complaint activity for the KneeFlex Total Knee System through June 15, 2020, including complaints received from April 1 through June 15 and year-to-date trend review. The analysis was completed in accordance with QP-820-014, Complaint Handling and Medical Device Reporting, using closed and open TrackWise records as of the extraction date.

Q2 Complaint Summary

A total of 23 KneeFlex complaints were received during the review period. Following duplicate review and preliminary coding, the principal categories are as follows:

| Complaint category | Q2 reports | Initial assessment |
|---|---:|---|
| Tibial tray loosening | 11 | Under clinical/product review; no common lot, size, or surgical site trend identified |
| Polyethylene wear debris | 4 | Consistent with known long-term wear profile; all cases involve patient/surgical factors requiring follow-up |
| Instrument breakage during surgery | 2 | Instrument complaints; contained to two separate procedural sets |
| Other / incomplete information | 6 | Pending additional records, product return, or closure as non-product related |

The eleven tibial tray loosening reports remain the largest category by count. Quality reviewed available implant duration, surgeon narratives, radiographs where supplied, and lot information. The cases are distributed across multiple tray sizes and manufacturing lots. At this time, the available information does not establish a recurring device failure mode. Several reports identify alignment, fixation technique, patient weight, or prior bone quality concerns as possible contributing factors, although those factors should not be treated as final conclusions until the clinical review is complete.

The four wear-debris reports have been routed for routine review with Post-Market Surveillance. Reported time to presentation is within the range anticipated for the relevant patient population and does not indicate an acute or unexpected increase. The two intraoperative instrument breakage reports have been sent to Operations for return analysis; neither involved a retained fragment or report of patient injury.

Complaint rates remain within the expected range when compared with available predicate-device complaint experience and KneeFlex’s current distribution base. There is no statistically meaningful increase in report frequency for the quarter, and no clustering by customer, geography, lot, or surgeon has been identified. No new MDR trend has been identified from this review. Individual event reporting decisions will continue to be made per procedure and documented in the associated TrackWise record.

Disposition

No CAPA is warranted this quarter. Quality will continue routine monthly surveillance of tibial tray loosening reports and will reassess if additional information identifies a common failure mechanism, a lot association, or a material change in rate. The instrument return analyses will be reviewed upon completion and included in the next quarterly trend package.

Please retain this memorandum with the Q2 PMS materials. Questions on specific records should be directed to Quality before any external characterization is made.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling

*Footnote: The complaint-handling workflow used for KneeFlex follows the same TrackWise intake process used for ApexHip under QP-820-014; this reference concerns procedure only and does not incorporate ApexHip complaint information into this analysis.*

Subject: Apex Revenue Impact Model - Q4 2022 Scenarios

Attached: Apex_Revenue_Impact_Model_Q4_2022_v5.xlsx

Owen,

Per our discussion, I refreshed the Apex model using September actuals and the current field forecast. The model is intended to frame revenue exposure through FY24; it does not attempt to estimate claim severity or timing.

Apex FY22 is now expected to close at approximately $71.0M, versus the $96.0M peak in FY20. The decline began before the June cup recall in the underlying order data. The more pronounced step-down follows the September 2021 labeling update and what Sales characterizes as increased surgeon caution after the NJR data circulated. The recall remains a separate, lot-specific assumption in the model, although several field teams report customers are not making that distinction.

Summary output ($M):

| Scenario | FY22E | FY23E | FY24E | FY22–FY24 Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Status quo / current label | 71.0 | 62.4 | 60.1 | (15%) |
| Label-driven decline | 71.0 | 54.7 | 45.9 | (35%) |
| Full market withdrawal | 71.0 | 48.3 | 42.6 | (40%) |

The status quo case assumes current labeling remains in place, no broad commercial action, and modest attrition offset by existing account utilization. It is the closest to the current Sales operating plan, though I would not characterize it as the base case with high confidence.

The label-driven decline case assumes continued loss of new implanters, lower utilization among accounts that have moved Apex to a limited-use position, and increasing price concessions where distributors seek to retain volume. This case reflects the present trajectory in the Southeast and selected Midwest accounts more closely than the operating plan.

The withdrawal case assumes no new commercial placements after an orderly market action, with only limited residual revenue from contracted inventory and replacement requirements. This is necessarily a planning construct, not a recommendation regarding product status.

For reserve adequacy testing, I recommend using the full withdrawal scenario as the conservative revenue sensitivity. It produces the lowest contribution available to absorb claims-related costs and avoids relying on a recovery in surgeon confidence that we are not seeing in the current forecast submissions.

I have kept the $18M Q3 reserve as a separate line item in the workbook and have not assumed any insurance recoveries. We can walk through the account-level assumptions Monday if helpful.

Hannah

RE: Urgent Quality and Safety Notification / Formal Product Complaint
ApexHip System: Recalled Inventory (Lot V-2247) and Unrelated Early Revisions

Dear Ms. Raman:

I am writing to formally log serious concerns regarding your ApexHip system. First, regarding the recent voluntary Class II recall notice we received dated June 14, 2022, my hospital's central sterile and incoming inspection team quarantined several components earlier this week. Specifically, an Apex acetabular cup from lot V-2247 showed visible coating delamination inside the sterile blister pack prior to presentation in the OR. The KinetiCoat porous surface was actively flaking off in small particulate fragments when the inner packaging was inspected.

This is unassisted flaking on unwrapping, which is completely unacceptable for an implant intended for immediate press-fit biological fixation. We have returned six unopened units from this lot to our local distributor per your recall instructions, but I demand an explicit accounting of what happened with your plasma-spray process and how this passed lot release.

Beyond this manufacturing recall, however, I must formally document two severe clinical failures involving ApexHip components implanted well prior to the recalled lot run. Both appear directly related to metal-on-metal wear and adverse local tissue reactions:

1. Patient D.K. (DOB 11/14/1963): Primary left total hip performed March 2019 (Cup Lot V-1892, 54mm; Head Lot H-3112, 44mm). Patient presented at 38 months post-op with groin pain and severe functional decline. Pre-op serum cobalt was 9.4 ppb; chromium was 8.1 ppb. During revision on June 18, 2022, I observed extensive metallosis, fluid-filled cystic collections, and abductor necrosis consistent with ARMD. The cup was well-fixed, but significant edge-wear was obvious on the bearing surface.

2. Patient R.M. (DOB 04/02/1958): Primary right total hip performed August 2018 (Cup Lot V-1644, 52mm; Head Lot H-3088, 40mm). Revised on June 27, 2022. The patient exhibited a 6 cm pseudotumor displacing the femoral neurovascular bundle. Explant revealed gross blackened fluid and extensive soft tissue destruction. Tissue samples confirmed severe histiocytic response and metal debris necrosis.

Both explant sets have been retained in formalin per standard hospital protocol and are available for your engineering team to analyze. Please provide immediate TrackWise reference numbers for these adverse events and confirm receipt of this correspondence.

Sincerely,

James M. Whitaker, MD
Mile High Orthopedic Specialists
Attending Orthopedic Surgeon, Denver Presbyterian Hospital

1. Purpose & Scope
This memorandum documents the Medical Device Reporting (MDR) reportability determination per internal procedure SOP-QA-404 (*Adverse Event Reporting and MDR Decision Trees*) and 21 CFR 803.50 for three recent complaint files originating from Dr. Marcus Feld’s clinical practice (Atlanta Joint Institute). All three cases involve the Veridian ApexHip Acetabular Cup system paired with Co/Cr modular heads.

2. File Assessments

A. TrackWise Record: TW-2018-0322
* Device Identification: ApexHip Cup, 52 mm (Lot V-2041); ApexHip Femoral Head, 40 mm (Lot H-3118). Implanted October 2017.
* Clinical Presentation: Patient presented at 10 months post-op with persistent groin pain, swelling, and reduced range of motion. Serum cobalt levels measured at 11.4 µg/L; chromium at 8.2 µg/L. Aspiration and MARS MRI revealed extensive local fluid collection and soft tissue inflammation consistent with metallosis. Dr. Feld has scheduled a revision surgery for October 4, 2018 to explant the acetabular and femoral bearing components.
* MDR Determination: REPORTABLE. Under 21 CFR 803.50(a)(1), this event constitutes a reportable serious injury. The event necessitated surgical intervention (revision arthroplasty) to preclude permanent impairment of a body structure/function resulting from local tissue reaction and adverse local tissue response (ALTR).

B. TrackWise Record: TW-2018-0340
* Device Identification: ApexHip Cup, 56 mm (Lot V-2044); ApexHip Femoral Head, 44 mm (Lot H-3142). Implanted December 2017.
* Clinical Presentation: Patient reported severe pain and gait instability at 8 months. Whole blood cobalt was confirmed at 14.1 µg/L. Ultrasound-guided aspiration recovered turbid, dark-stained synovial fluid indicative of metal debris. Operative notes from Dr. Feld recommend urgent revision due to progressive tissue necrosis and pseudotumor formation.
* MDR Determination: REPORTABLE. In accordance with 21 CFR 803.50, this case satisfies the criteria for serious injury requiring medical/surgical intervention to prevent irreversible tissue damage.

C. TrackWise Record: TW-2018-0311
* Device Identification: ApexHip Cup, 50 mm (Lot V-2039); ApexHip Femoral Head, 38 mm (Lot H-3094). Implanted September 2017.

* MDR Determination: NON-REPORTABLE AT THIS TIME (HELD PENDING DATA). The current clinical presentation does not meet the serious injury threshold under 21 CFR 803.3. File is held pending secondary laboratory cobalt retest data and clinical follow-up records from the clinic, expected by September 24, 2018.

3. Action Items
1. Quality has updated the MDR disposition blocks in TrackWise for TW-2018-0322 and TW-2018-0340 to "Reportable."
2. Recommend Devon Mitchell prepare draft initial FDA Form 3500A submissions for lots V-2041 and V-2044 to ensure timely submission within the 30-day statutory clock.

Subject: AJRR Q3 2021 data pull - ApexHip revision trend

Priya, Dana—

Following up on last week’s Registry Signal Review, I completed the Q3 AJRR pull using the same inclusion criteria we discussed: primary ApexHip procedures with at least 24 months of follow-up, compared with the available peer metal-on-metal cohort.

The AJRR data corroborate the direction of the March NJR findings. The absolute numbers are smaller and the confidence intervals are wider than NJR, but Apex is showing an elevated all-cause revision rate relative to peer MoM systems in the AJRR extract. The separation is most apparent in the 36–60 month follow-up band.

A few points from the stratification:

- The revision signal appears concentrated in the larger head sizes, particularly 44–50 mm. Smaller-head cases do not show the same degree of separation, although the case counts are limited.
- Where cup inclination was available in the registry record, revised Apex cases were disproportionately represented above approximately 50 degrees.
- That pattern is directionally consistent with Tom Halvorsen’s 2019 high-inclination wear work. I am not suggesting the registry establishes causation; it does, however, make the edge-loading hypothesis difficult to dismiss as a laboratory-only finding.
- Revision indications remain variably coded. Pain, elevated metal ions, adverse local tissue reaction, and “other mechanical” are all present, so I would avoid relying on any single indication category without chart-level review.

I have attached the summary workbook, including the denominator definitions, exclusions, and a tab showing the inclination/head-size subset. I also included the NJR figures for reference, but did not combine the registries analytically.

Please let me know whether you want the underlying case-level list routed to Quality for complaint cross-checking. My recommendation remains that we maintain a recurring monthly review through the label-update period rather than wait for the next annual registry publication.

Greg

Attachment: AJRR_Q3_2021_ApexHip_summary.xlsx

MEMORANDUM

Date: 12 April 2022
From: Bill Kowalski, Plant Manager, Cork
To: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs
Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer, ApexHip
Subject: Preliminary Root Cause Assessment — KinetiCoat Adhesion Failures, Cup Lots V-2200 through V-2299

Priya, Dana, Tom —

Following up on the two incoming-inspection complaints (Northgate Health System and the Denver facility) regarding flaking of the KinetiCoat porous titanium coating on unwrapped acetabular cups, the line investigation team here has completed our preliminary root cause review. I want to get this in front of you before we go further so we can talk timing on any containment action.

Background: on 18 November 2021 we performed scheduled preventive maintenance on plasma-spray chamber 2 (the chamber used for essentially all cup coating runs from that date forward). Part of that maintenance involved replacement of the torch nozzle assembly and recalibration of the gas flow controllers. Our post-maintenance verification at the time checked flow rates and confirmed the chamber was "in spec" per the standard startup checklist, but that checklist does not independently verify chamber temperature ramp behavior or the standoff distance (nozzle-to-substrate gap) under sustained production conditions — only at idle. Our engineering team's review of the process data historian shows a slow drift in both chamber temperature (running roughly 15–20°C above the historical mean during long runs) and standoff distance (drifting outward by approximately 1.5–2 mm from the qualified setpoint) beginning almost immediately after the November maintenance and continuing undetected until the chamber was next serviced in early February 2022.

This drift window corresponds closely to production of cup lots V-2200 through V-2299.

Bond strength testing (per our internal pull-test method, spec minimum 20 MPa) on retained samples pulled from the affected date range confirms the concern. Results below.

Lot / Test Bond Strength
V-2214 / 13.1 MPa
V-2231 / 12.0 MPa
V-2248 / 14.6 MPa
V-2267 / 11.8 MPa
V-2284 / 15.3 MPa
V-2192 (pre-drift, control) / 26.4 MPa
V-2305 (post-repair, control) / 24.9 MPa

As you can see, every affected lot we've pulled samples from tests well below the 20 MPa specification, with values as low as 11.8–12.0 MPa. Lots manufactured before the November maintenance event and after the February re-service both test comfortably in the 24–28 MPa range, consistent with our historical process capability. This is a strong signal that the maintenance event itself is the root cause, not a raw material or supplier issue — incoming titanium powder lots for this period test within normal specification and show no anomalies.

We have not yet identified why the post-maintenance verification checklist failed to catch the drift; that's a separate CAPA item on our end and I'll have more for you on the checklist gap by end of month.

Recommendations:

1. Quarantine all remaining Cork and Warsaw inventory of cup lots V-2200 through V-2299 pending final disposition. I've already instructed the warehouse here to segregate what we have on-site.
2. Priya, I'd ask Quality to coordinate with Dana's team on whether this warrants a field action given units already distributed — 1,140 units went out the door in this lot range per our shipping records, and we don't yet know how many are implanted.
3. Tom, if you have bandwidth, it would help to have Design confirm there's no interaction between the coating adhesion issue and the wear characteristics you've been looking at — I want to be clear these appear to be independent failure modes, but I know that question will come up.

I'll have the full root cause report, including corrective action plan for chamber 2 monitoring going forward, by the end of next week. Happy to get on a call before then if useful.

Bill

Bill Kowalski
Plant Manager, Cork
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

Veridian Orthopedics — Reconstructive Sales
Q1 2022 Objection Handling Refresh: Recall Context
Prepared by: Carlos Mendes, Product Manager, ApexHip
Date: January 11, 2022
Distribution: Reconstructive sales team (internal use only — do not forward externally)

Purpose
As we prep the field for potential questions ahead of any customer-facing communications on the cup lot matter, I want to make sure everyone is drawing a clean line between two separate topics. We've seen some blending of these in call notes and I want to nip that before it becomes a pattern.

Two distinct issues — keep them separate

1. Coating/lot issue (Cork manufacturing) — a limited number of acetabular cup lots (V-2200 through V-2299, produced Nov 2021–Feb 2022) showed a coating adhesion irregularity identified during incoming inspection at two facilities. This is a manufacturing quality matter tied to a specific production window. Quality and Regulatory are running lot traceability now; more to follow from Dana's team on timing/scope.

2. Bearing surface / revision rate discussion — this is the ongoing, industry-wide conversation around metal-on-metal wear performance and registry data (NJR, AJRR) that surgeons have been raising since last fall. That's a separate clinical topic and is already addressed in the FAQ Priya's and Dana's teams sent out in September, along with the Dear Doctor letter and label update language.

Suggested script if asked
"This is a manufacturing quality issue with a specific batch, separate from the industry-wide bearing surface discussion. We identified it through our own inspection process and are addressing it directly with affected accounts. It's not related to the wear performance questions you may have seen in the registry data — that's a separate topic we've already given you materials on."

Do
- Refer back to the September FAQ for revision-rate/registry questions.
- Keep coating questions focused on lot numbers, not wear mechanism.
- Loop in your RSM if a surgeon pushes on both topics at once.

Don't
- Speculate on root cause beyond "manufacturing process deviation under review."
- Use the words "recall" or "withdrawal" until we have official notice language — more on that soon.

Questions to me or Jenna. Thanks for staying disciplined on this — it matters.

From: Leon Adeyemi <ladeyemi@veridianortho.com>
To: Dana Okonkwo <dokonkwo@veridianortho.com>, Rob Castellano <rcastellano@veridianortho.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2021 14:22:15 -0400
Subject: Follow-up on Registry Signal Review decision

Rob, Dana,

I am writing to formally record my clinical reservations following Tuesday's Registry Signal Review meeting. While I appreciate the commercial imperative behind maintaining market availability and proceeding with a labeling update, I remain uneasy about the risk profile we are asking surgeons and patients to accept.

The UK National Joint Registry’s 7.1% five-year revision rate is more than double the class average of 3.2%. From a clinical standpoint, this is not an anomaly that can be dismissed as surgical technique alone. When coupled with Tom Halvorsen’s 2019 internal simulator data—which demonstrated a 4–6x increase in volumetric wear at a 55-degree inclination angle compared to the standard 45-degree ISO 14242 protocol—we have a coherent biomechanical explanation for the adverse local tissue reactions being reported.

If we proceed with distributing a "Dear Doctor" letter next month, I strongly advise that we present the elevated revision signal and steep inclination wear characteristics transparently, rather than softening the communication with generic safe-use advisory language. Surgeons need clear, unvarnished clinical facts to properly monitor their existing cohort.

Finally, I request that we calendar a mandatory follow-up signal review in six months to re-evaluate the registry trajectories and AJRR data.

Regards,

Leon

Leon Adeyemi, MD
Chief Medical Officer
Veridian Orthopedics, Inc.

Post-Market Surveillance Memorandum

Date: June 5, 2023
From: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
To: File
Subject: Registry and complaint correlation memo - pre-MDL summary

This memorandum summarizes the relationship between external registry findings and Veridian’s internal ApexHip complaint and MDR trending through the current reporting period. I prepared this as a consolidated reference because we should expect requests for this material as the pending state-court matters develop and, potentially, are coordinated.

The short version is that the registry and complaint datasets have been directionally consistent since 2019. They are not interchangeable datasets, and neither proves causation on its own. However, both show a pattern of earlier-than-expected revision in a subset of ApexHip patients, with metal-ion findings, adverse local tissue reactions, and revision narratives that are consistent with a wear-related mechanism.

1. Registry findings

The March 2021 UK National Joint Registry annual report identified a five-year ApexHip revision rate of 7.1%, compared with a 3.2% class average for the relevant total-hip population. The NJR data have limitations: it does not provide complete patient-level laboratory values, surgeon technique variables are incompletely captured, and the product cohort is materially smaller than the aggregate comparator group. Nonetheless, the direction and magnitude of the difference warranted the September 2021 Registry Signal Review.

AJRR extracts received in late 2021 similarly showed an elevated revision signal for Apex relative to comparable contemporary total hips. The AJRR data were less mature than the NJR dataset at that time, and the confidence intervals were wider. The mid-2022 AJRR refresh did not eliminate the signal. Rather, it continued to show higher revision incidence in the Apex cohort, particularly in cases coded with pain, metallosis/metal-debris terminology, instability, or aseptic loosening. Coding practices vary by site, so these categories should not be treated as clinical adjudications.

2. Internal complaints and MDRs

TrackWise complaint entries first showed a meaningful cluster in 2018, including three metal-ion-related complaints from Atlanta-area patients treated in Dr. Feld’s practice. By 2019, the internal trend reports reflected increasing reports of elevated cobalt and chromium, pain, fluid collections, tissue reaction, and early revision. Not all reported cases contained complete records or confirmed implant component details. Several were initially coded under broad pain or revision categories before follow-up information was received.

The MDR population follows the same general trajectory. Reportable events increased as revisions and explant findings were received, although MDR timing should not be read as event timing because of reporting lags, supplemental records, and follow-up. The internal complaint/MDR trend is therefore most useful when reviewed by implant date and event date, where available, rather than filing date alone.

3. Mechanism assessment

The pattern is consistent with the edge-loading wear mechanism identified by Tom Halvorsen’s engineering team in the 2019 re-analysis of Apex wear testing. At 55-degree cup inclination, the testing showed approximately four- to six-fold increased wear relative to the standard 45-degree protocol. The clinical and registry data do not establish cup inclination for every affected patient, and patient, surgical, and implant variables may contribute. Still, elevated Co/Cr results and ARMD-type findings in the complaint records are directionally aligned with the engineering explanation and with the registry revision signal.

This conclusion is separate from the 2022 KinetiCoat cup-lot recall. The recalled V-2200 through V-2299 lots concern coating adhesion and a manufacturing parameter drift at Cork; they should not be combined analytically with the metal-ion/wear signal absent a case-specific basis.

Recommendation: Quality and PMS should finalize the Apex complaint database, including the current reconciliation of duplicate and follow-up records, and maintain a cross-reference between complaint/MDR records and the applicable NJR and AJRR citations. Any external response should clearly identify data-source limitations, reporting lags, and the distinction between the coating recall and the wear-related issue.

MEMORANDUM

TO: Post-Market Surveillance Committee; Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs; Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
FROM: Greg Novak, Director, Post-Market Surveillance
DATE: June 1, 2020
SUBJECT: KneeFlex Total Knee System — Post-Market Surveillance Summary (Q2 2020)

1. Purpose & Scope
This memorandum summarizes the routine post-market clinical follow-up and surveillance data for the KneeFlex Total Knee System for the second quarter of 2020, covering cumulative commercial experience from launch (October 2019) through May 15, 2020.

2. Surveillance Methodology
The surveillance protocols applied in this review utilize the standardized Veridian Post-Market Surveillance Registry Integration Protocol (SOP-PMS-042). This methodology mirrors the active surveillance workflows currently deployed across all Veridian reconstructive joint product lines, including our primary hip portfolios (ClassicHip and ApexHip) and ShoulderPro. Specifically, internal complaint intake from TrackWise is cross-indexed against quarterly dataset releases from the American Joint Replacement Registry (AJRR) and regional hospital purchasing registries, applying cumulative incidence estimates and survivorship modeling (Kaplan-Meier analysis).

3. Registry & Complaint Findings
To date, commercial distribution of KneeFlex has reached an estimated 4,820 implanted units across the United States.

- Cumulative Revision Rate: KneeFlex currently demonstrates an all-cause cumulative revision rate of 1.8% at roughly 8 months of follow-up. By comparison, the aggregate AJRR class benchmark for contemporary cruciate-retaining and posterior-stabilized total knee arthroplasty systems stands at 3.2% for equivalent timepoints.
- Primary Revision Drivers: Among the limited verified revisions reported in TrackWise (n=14), primary failure modes are distributed as follows:
  * Infection / Septic Loosening: 8 cases (57.1%)
  * Periprosthetic Fracture (traumatic): 4 cases (28.6%)
  * Instability / Sizing Mismatch: 2 cases (14.3%)
- Mechanical & Wear Metrics: There have been zero reports of tibial insert disassociation, premature polyethylene delamination, or abnormal metallic debris generation.

4. Registry Signals
No statistically significant performance or safety outliers have been detected across any age cohort or patient demographic. The funnel plot analysis for KneeFlex across high-volume participating institutions remains well within the 95% and 99.8% control limits. No registry safety alerts, outlier notices, or external trending inquiries have been issued by AJRR or regulatory bodies regarding this system.

5. Summary & Next Steps
KneeFlex continues to perform exceptionally well in early post-market tracking, tracking comfortably below competitive revision baselines. Standard surveillance will continue per the established schedule, with the next formal registry pull scheduled for September 2020 ahead of the Q3 PMS Committee review. No changes to the Risk Management File, Instructions for Use (IFU), or clinical evaluation plans are recommended at this time.

VERIDIAN ORTHOPEDICS, INC.
MEMORANDUM

Date: June 20, 2024
From: Owen Park, Chief Financial Officer
Subject: End-of-Period Financial Summary - ApexHip Product Line Closure

This memorandum summarizes Finance’s current view of the ApexHip product line through June 30, 2024, including historical contribution, withdrawal-related charges, and the contingent-liability outlook. It is intended as a closing-period reference for the product line; the underlying legal and claims matters remain open.

ApexHip was launched in the United States in April 2017, following 510(k) clearance, and in Europe in September 2017. It achieved rapid adoption in its intended active-adult segment and became a material contributor to Reconstructive revenue. The line reached peak annual sales in 2020, when approximately 14,200 systems generated revenue of approximately $96 million. That represented roughly 22% of consolidated company revenue for that year.

Based on booked sales through withdrawal and remaining recognized revenue, Finance estimates cumulative ApexHip lifetime revenue of approximately $410 million for the 2017 through 2024 period. This estimate includes U.S. and international sales and is subject to routine quarter-end revenue adjustments, returns, credits, and distributor true-ups. The February 2, 2024 voluntary market withdrawal ended new commercial sales activity, although certain post-withdrawal customer credits, field inventory returns, and service-related transactions continue to be processed.

The financial impact of ApexHip has developed in stages. In the third quarter of 2022, the Company recorded an $18 million reserve for Apex-related claims. At that time, the reserve reflected known and reasonably estimable exposure, including then-pending claims activity, anticipated defense costs, and available information regarding product allegations. It did not represent a final estimate of ultimate loss.

As additional claims were filed and the federal proceeding developed, Finance’s internal range increased. During 2023 and the first half of 2024, working estimates generally placed the potential Company-funded exposure in a range of $45 million to $70 million, depending on assumptions concerning case inventory, dismissal rates, indemnity allocation, defense costs, insurance recoveries, and the timing and structure of any global resolution.

MDL 3102 currently includes approximately 520 filed cases and continues to grow. Case count alone is not a measure of ultimate liability; however, the pace of filings, claimant medical profiles, revision status, and the cost of ongoing coordinated litigation have been incorporated into our reserve analyses. Finance will continue to coordinate with Legal, Quality, Regulatory, and our outside advisors as additional case-specific information becomes available.

For planning purposes, management is evaluating a proposed settlement contribution of $80 million from Veridian, combined with a tentative $40 million coverage contribution from Aegis Specialty. These figures remain subject to negotiation, policy analysis, allocation discussions, and agreement on a mediation framework. They should not be understood as a completed settlement, a final coverage determination, or a fixed accounting conclusion. Aegis’s participation remains tentative, and any recovery will depend on finalized terms and applicable policy conditions.

The total financial effect of ApexHip therefore includes more than the product-line reserve. It also encompasses withdrawal costs, customer credits, inventory-related charges, continuing defense expense, and internal support costs. Those elements will continue to be tracked separately where practical so that reserve movements are not conflated with ordinary operational closeout expenses.

Finance will continue quarterly reserve reviews until the mediation framework is finalized and all claims are resolved. Any material change in the expected Veridian contribution, Aegis participation, case inventory, or accounting treatment will be brought forward through the standard quarter-end review process.

Owen Park
Chief Financial Officer

MEMORANDUM

Date: June 22, 2015
From: Tom Halvorsen, Sr. Design Engineer
To: Priya Raman; Carlos Mendes
Subject: ApexHip concept design kickoff notes

Priya, Carlos —

putting down some notes from the concept kickoff last week so we have a starting point before design inputs get locked. this is early, still moving fast, expect changes.

Basic concept: total hip system, Co/Cr femoral head and stem (same alloy family as ClassicHip, proven manufacturing route), paired with an acetabular cup using the new titanium porous coating we picked up in the KBT deal. calling it KinetiCoat internally for now unless marketing wants something else (carlos - your call). the coating is the differentiator here, better bone ingrowth than our current sintered bead surface, that's the whole pitch for going metal-on-metal with this generation.

Target design inputs, draft:

- head diameters: 36mm to 50mm, in 2mm increments. larger heads for stability/ROM, which is a selling point for the "active" patient segment we keep talking about.
- cup sizes: 44mm to 62mm, matching head range plus offset options
- wear rate target: below ClassicHip benchmark (we'll pull the actual number from the ClassicHip DHF, I think Priya has that on file, need the polyethylene wear data as our comparator even though we're going MoM here, different failure mode obviously but leadership wants an apples-to-apples number for the design input doc)
- inclination range for cup placement: still nailing this down, but leaning toward specifying the standard 40-45 degree range surgeons are trained on. more on that below.

Open item — wear test protocol: we haven't picked a standard yet. ISO 14242 is the obvious baseline, that's what everybody uses and what FDA will expect to see referenced. question is whether we test at a single inclination angle or run a matrix across angles to see how sensitive the wear rate is to cup positioning in the OR, since surgeons don't all hit the same angle every time. I lean toward doing at least a sensitivity check but that adds time and cost to the test campaign. want to get Priya's read on this from a quality/DHF standpoint before I bring it to DR-2.

Timeline: aiming to have design inputs finalized and formally approved by September 2015. That gives us runway to hit DR-3 later this year for the wear test protocol decision and start locking down the coating spec with the KBT engineers (their due diligence notes mentioned they don't have a ton of long-term adhesion data yet, so we'll want to build that into our own verification plan rather than just leaning on their historical data).

Carlos — will need your input on head/cup size matrix vs. what sales thinks the market wants, and whether 50mm heads are overkill or a selling point.

Let's grab 30 min next week to align before I write this up formally.

Tom

MEETING MINUTES

Meeting: Apex Coating Issue Field Action Decision Meeting
Date: April 21, 2022
Time: 10:00–11:15 a.m. ET
Location: Teams / Warsaw Hub, Conference Room 4B
Prepared by: Dana Okonkwo, VP Regulatory Affairs

Attendees: Dana Okonkwo, Priya Raman, Bill Kowalski, Rachel Steinberg, Carlos Mendes, Owen Park

Purpose
To review the KinetiCoat adhesion issue affecting certain ApexHip acetabular cup lots and determine the appropriate field action.

Discussion Summary

Mr. Kowalski reviewed Cork manufacturing records and the preliminary investigation. The affected population is cup lots V-2200 through V-2299, manufactured following the plasma-spray chamber maintenance event. The current evidence supports parameter drift during the relevant production period as the probable cause of insufficient KinetiCoat adhesion. The observed failure mode is coating flaking or separation identified on unwrapping during incoming inspection at two hospital customers.

Ms. Raman confirmed that the distribution reconciliation currently identifies 1,140 affected units distributed. Of those, 412 are recorded as implanted. The remaining units are believed to be in hospital inventory, distributor inventory, or otherwise pending confirmation through the effectiveness process. Quality will continue reconciliation as customer responses are received.

The group agreed that the product should be removed from distribution and that a voluntary Class II recall is warranted for lots V-2200 through V-2299. Regulatory will proceed on that basis, subject to final review of the notification package and lot list.

For avoidance of doubt, the scope of this field action is limited to the KinetiCoat adhesion/manufacturing issue associated with the identified cup lots. Metal-ion levels, wear performance, ARMD, registry data, and other metal-on-metal concerns were expressly noted as outside the scope of this action. Those matters are being addressed through their respective Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, and Regulatory processes and should not be characterized in customer communications as the basis for this recall.

Ms. Okonkwo advised that the target for recall initiation should be mid-June 2022, allowing time for completion of the health hazard evaluation, final lot tracing, customer lists, and FDA notification materials. Ms. Steinberg requested that communications remain factual and limited to the identified coating adhesion condition, the affected lots, and the customer instructions.

Mr. Mendes noted that Sales will require a concise field script and FAQ once the customer letter is approved. Ms. Raman stated that the initial hospital notification should instruct customers to identify, quarantine, and return unused affected cups, while providing a contact path for questions regarding implanted devices. No clinical recommendation language will be included without Regulatory and clinical review.

Mr. Park confirmed that Finance will begin modeling the anticipated reserve, including return logistics, replacement product, customer notification, and potential claim exposure. He asked Quality to provide a weekly update on the distributed/implanted reconciliation.

Action Items

1. Dana Okonkwo — Draft FDA voluntary recall notification, health hazard evaluation, and associated Regulatory package. Target: May 6, 2022.
2. Priya Raman — Prepare hospital notification letter, distribution list, return instructions, and effectiveness-check process. Target: May 13, 2022.
3. Bill Kowalski — Complete Cork batch-record review and provide final affected-lot confirmation and root-cause documentation. Target: April 29, 2022.
4. Owen Park — Begin financial reserve modeling based on 1,140 distributed units and 412 implanted units; update as reconciliation changes. Target: May 6, 2022.
5. Carlos Mendes — Prepare draft Sales FAQ and field communication plan after Quality/Regulatory approve customer language. Target: May 20, 2022.
6. Rachel Steinberg — Review external communications and recall materials before issuance. Target: upon receipt of drafts.

Subject: RE: Revised brochure claim: "proven long-term durability"

Carlos, Anika,

I do not support “proven long-term durability.”

Sales growth and favorable anecdotal feedback from surgeons are not clinical proof, and neither substitutes for follow-up data. We have approximately 18 months of post-market experience, not long-term survivorship evidence. The design rationale may be sound, but that is a different claim.

I recommend:

“ApexHip is engineered for durability and stability for active adults.”

If Marketing wants to retain the lifetime-of-movement concept, it should be reviewed separately; I would avoid tying it to durability until we have meaningful registry data and longer clinical follow-up.

Please do not characterize Feld’s or other early users’ impressions as proof in brochure copy. We can revisit stronger language when the registry data mature.

Leon

From: Priya Raman, Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
To: Quality Systems, Regulatory Affairs, Document Control
Subject: ClassicHip DHF archival procedure

Effective immediately, the ClassicHip design history file will be transferred from active Agile access to controlled archival storage following discontinuation of the ClassicHip product line.

This procedure applies to the completed ClassicHip DHF, including design plans, design inputs and outputs, verification and validation records, design reviews, risk-management files, engineering change orders, labeling approvals, manufacturing transfer documentation, and associated DHF index records. Document Control remains responsible for confirming that the archived file is complete, legible, indexed, and retrievable before the active project workspace is closed.

Per Veridian document retention policy QP-DC-014 and applicable Quality System Regulation requirements, ClassicHip DHF records must be retained for a minimum of fifteen (15) years from the date the product line was discontinued, or longer where required by an applicable regulatory, contractual, or legal requirement. No original controlled record may be destroyed, overwritten, or removed from the archive during the retention period without approval from Quality Systems and Regulatory Affairs.

The archival package will consist of:

1. The final Agile DHF export, including revision history and approval metadata.
2. The current DHF index and document-status report.
3. A records transfer checklist signed by Document Control and Quality.
4. Any paper originals identified in the DHF index as controlled originals.
5. A retrieval cross-reference identifying the Agile project number and archive box or electronic folder location.

Electronic records will be retained in the read-only Quality Records repository, under:

Hub Records Center / Product Archives / ClassicHip / DHF Final Archive

Paper originals, where applicable, will be boxed, labeled “ClassicHip DHF — Controlled Archive,” and transferred to the Hub Records Center at 4400 Silver Lake Blvd., Warsaw. Box identifiers must be entered into the Records Center inventory log before transfer.

Requests for archived records should be submitted through Document Control. Retrievals must preserve the archived record’s integrity and chain of custody. Any copy provided for review must be marked uncontrolled unless issued through the applicable document-control process.

Please complete the transfer checklist and provide confirmation of archive completion to Quality Systems by February 23.

Priya Raman
Director, Quality & Complaint Handling
